person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should
contact the City Clerk’s Office at (909) 596-8726 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

The Council Chambers will be open to the public at 6:00 p.m. Materials related to an item on this agenda,
submitted to the Planning Commission after distribution of the agenda packet, are available for public inspection
at the meeting or in the Community Development Department during normal business hours.

Agenda Report
DATE:  November 8, 2023

TO:  Planning Commission

FROM:  Parker Stringfellow, Assistant Planner

SUBJECT:  Case Number 111-23VAR – 2034 Cottage Place – A Request for a
  Variance from the Two-Car Garage Requirement Prior to a Living Space
  Addition to a Single-Family Home

SUMMARY
This application is a request for a variance from the requirement of a two-car garage to
allow for an addition to the rear of a one story single-family detached home located at
2034 Cottage Place. The proposed addition cannot be approved without the provision of
a two-car garage required by the La Verne Municipal Code for residential parking, or
without the granting of this variance.

RECOMMENDATION
Based on the findings in this report and the conditions of approval in the draft resolution
(Attachment 1), staff recommends that the Planning approve Case No. 111-23VAR by
adopting Resolution No 1314.

Staff will update the Planning Commission at the meeting with the Development Review
Committee’s recommendation.

DISCUSSION
2034 Cottage Place is a unique property in La Verne in that it is one of only three parcels
whose only frontage to the public right-of-way is on Cottage Place, the only alleyway in
the City that is named (Attachment 2). These parcels are also smaller in size, have
uneven side property line lengths and curved rear (north) property lines which abut the
Live Oak Wash. Further, 2034 Cottage Place is one of only two properties whose
residential structures directly front the alleyway, have smaller setbacks to the front
property lines, and are built out to side property line setbacks.

Property owners Eric and Mariah Odegaard inquired with staff about adding living space
onto the rear of their home. As it exists today, it is a modest 864 square foot home with
two bedrooms and one-bathroom, and the owners would like to add another bedroom
and bathroom (578 square feet), for a total of three bedrooms and two bathrooms
(Attachments 3 & 4). The concept appears to meet all the development standards except
for a garage. Staff explained to the owners that the La Verne Municipal Code requires
that all single-family homes have a fully enclosed two-car garage with minimum interior
dimensions of 20’ by 20’, and that no living space additions can be approved without it,
or without a variance.
 Case No. 111-23VAR – 2034 Cottage Place
November 8, 2023
Page 2

Due to the placement of the existing house on the lot, the only space available on the lot
to build a garage is the rear yard, which is inaccessible from the Cottage Place frontage.
This physical constraint makes it impossible to provide the required garage without severe
modification to the existing structure, therefore staff supports the request for a variance
from the garage requirement to allow the proposed addition.

COMPATIBILITY WITH SURROUNDING USES
The project site is located within the PR4.5D zoning district and is surrounded by single-
family residences on either side, as well as across the alley to the south, and across the
Live Oak Wash to the north.

If the variance is granted and the project can proceed, staff will work with the applicant to
ensure all development standards are met, including matching architectural style and
materials of the existing structure. Staff has included a condition of approval requiring the
retention of existing parking facilities on-site so as to not worsen the vehicular
access/parking situation for the property, and no negative impacts with the construction
of the proposed addition are expected.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS
This project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act per Section 15303
in that the issuance of the variance would allow for the addition of 578 square feet to an
existing single family dwelling. No further environmental review is required at this time.

Dear Planning Commission:

We are requesting a variance to add 578 square feet to the back of our home without adding a
400-square-foot garage. The home addition would increase the living space and would add a
bedroom and bathroom. Two sycamore trees are located just north of our home, the closest of
which sits 8 feet from the northern wall of our home. To have adequate space to complete the
addition, we need to remove the trees. At approximately 21 inches and 26 inches respectively,
the trunks of both trees are smaller than the 36-inch limit that would require a permit. We also
do not have a garage on our property, and due to its unusual location, adding a garage would
not be feasible. Our street, Cottage Place, is both an alley and a street. It is the only street in La
Verne in this situation. While there are street addresses, our street is, for all intents and
purposes, an alley due to our distance from the properties across from us, due to its lack of a
curb or sidewalk, and due to its location in relation to Seventh Street. Our addition project merits
a variance for three key reasons:

  1) Unlike most homes in the immediate vicinity, our house does not have access to an alley
  because the service road south of the Live Oak Wash forms the northern boundary of
  our property. Because this service road is on LA County land, we cannot access it to use
  it as a thoroughfare for any potential garage.
  2) There is no room in the front (i.e., the south side) of the property to build a garage. The
  house sits so far forward in the lot that our carport and driveway make up almost the
  entirety of the front yard. Were we to build a garage in that location, we wouldn’t have
  space for a driveway. The garage would have to abut the street, and the garage door
  would be situated on the border of the street and our property. Therefore, there would be
  no way for drivers to determine if there was oncoming traffic when they exit the garage,
  which would pose a significant safety hazard.
  3) We can’t add a detached garage in the backyard because there isn’t enough room to
  build the necessary driveway leading to it. Because the house was built in 1956, the side
  setbacks of our house currently do not conform to code. On the east side, there is only 5
  feet between our house and the next property. On the west side, we have only 8 to 9 feet
  clearance, a space that is much too narrow to accommodate even a small vehicle.

We wouldn’t ask for a variance unless it was absolutely necessary. We feel that the reasons
listed above are sufficient to merit your consideration. Thank you for your time.

Sincerely,

Mariah and Eric Odegaard
